description:
We are TEAM MAX-H, where space data meets human imagination.
Our team brings together coding, design, and storytelling.
For the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, we aim to turn archival data into immersive stories.
We want to connect people with the missions and discoveries they may never have heard of.
Our goal: make space history something people don’t just learn—but feel.
summary:
Abandoned But Not Forgotten is an interactive web experience and animated story developed by TEAM MAX-H, told from the perspective of humanity’s retired robotic explorers—silent pioneers resting across the Moon, Mars, and deep space.

Using verified NASA mission archives, we created a three-chapter narrative experience covering Chapter 1: The Moon (Apollo 11’s Eagle & Surveyor 3), Chapter 2: Mars (Mars Pathfinder & Sojourner), and Chapter 3: Deep Space (Pioneer 10 & Pioneer 11). Instead of dense technical reports, our platform transforms complex aerospace data into relatable, Gen-Z-friendly animated dialogues and visual timelines designed for teenagers, students, and everyday space enthusiasts.

Once their transmissions fade, retired spacecraft are often forgotten—yet they paved the way for modern spaceflight and interstellar exploration. By blending accurate NASA science with expressive visual storytelling, our project ensures the trailblazers that opened the solar system are never forgotten by the next generation.
details:
Abandoned But Not Forgotten is an interactive, Gen-Z-friendly space storytelling web platform and 3-chapter animated video series developed by TEAM MAX-H to bring humanity’s retired robotic space explorers back into the spotlight.

🔗 PROJECT LINKS:

• Interactive Web App — Chapter 1 (Moon Tellers: Apollo 11 Eagle & Surveyor 3): https://moon-lunar-mission-relay-1.ai.studio/

• Interactive Web Platform — Chapter 2 (Mars Tellers: Pathfinder & Sojourner): https://abandoned-but-not-forgotten-website.vercel.app/

• Full 3-Chapter Animated Storytelling Film (YouTube — Moon, Mars & Deep Space): https://youtu.be/tZkEp3vXbes?si=NkYy7Ee4OGsvRIV5

🚀 WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS:

Instead of presenting static, intimidating technical archives, our platform lets users explore space history through interactive web chapters and expressive animated dialogues where the spacecraft themselves tell their stories:

• Chapter 1 — The Moon (Apollo 11’s Eagle & Surveyor 3): Explores Surveyor 3’s 1967 landing in the Ocean of Storms, its lunar soil-digging experiments, Apollo 11 Eagle’s nearby 1969 touchdown, and Apollo 12’s historic visit to retrieve Surveyor 3’s camera.

• Chapter 2 — Mars (Mars Pathfinder & Sojourner): Highlights the 1997 Ares Vallis landing and how the microwave-sized Sojourner rover analyzed Martian rocks, proving mobile planetary exploration was possible.

• Chapter 3 — Deep Space (Pioneer 10 & Pioneer 11): Follows NASA’s twin trailblazers launched during a rare 175-year planetary alignment—powered by Plutonium-238 RTGs, crossing the Asteroid Belt, capturing the first close-ups of Jupiter and Saturn, carrying Carl Sagan’s Golden Plaque, and drifting into interstellar space (with Pioneer 10 reaching 7.6 billion miles before its final signal in 2003).

💡 BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT:

• Democratizes Space Science: Bridges the gap between complex NASA telemetry and young learners by turning verified facts into memorable, conversational storytelling.

• Preserves Space Heritage: Ensures students and future explorers remember the foundational robotic pioneers that made modern missions like Perseverance and Voyager possible.

🛠️ TOOLS, TECHNOLOGIES & SOFTWARE USED:

• Web Development & Deployment: Gemini , Origin kit , v0.com , Bolt.new , ElevenLabs.

• Visuals, 3D Animation & Video Production:Google AI Studio and CapCut for video editing, subtitles, and sound design.

• Data Sources: Official NASA Science mission archives (Surveyor 3, Apollo 11, Mars Pathfinder, Sojourner, Pioneer 10, and Pioneer 11).

🎨 CREATIVITY & KEY DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS:

• First-Person Spacecraft Perspective: Giving real engineering facts (like RTG power, radiation belts, and orbital trajectories) a warm, relatable Gen-Z voice makes technical data emotionally engaging.

• Accessibility & Accuracy: Our team balanced beginner-friendly language with 100% NASA-verified timelines, launch dates, and distances, ensuring zero scientific compromises while keeping the interface clean, responsive, and easy to navigate on any device.
